title: Difference between pair creation and anomaly matching: Nontrivial aspects of invertible symmetries and defects in $SU(N)$ models
abstract: We study the connection between the $SU(N)_{K}$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and $SU(N)_{K'}$ WZW models, enforcing the unbroken $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ symmetries. The fundamental underlying structures are the (half-)integer spin simple currents in the topological quantum field theories and anomaly matching conditions in conformal field theories. For the (half-)integer spin simple current condition of the folded models $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} \overline{SU(N)_{K'}}$ or $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} SU(N)_{K'}$, we obtain the generalized pairing condition $K= \pm R^{2}K' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=1$. On the other hand, the anomaly matching condition results in the weaker condition $K= \pm RUK' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=\text{gcd}(U,N)=1$. Surprisingly, the anomaly matching without the pairing condition results in the intrinsic mismatch of the preservation law of the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ defects and symmetries. The pairing condition canonically relates symmetries and defects, as in category theory, whereas it is unclear whether it can be a guiding principle in prohibiting the massless renormalization group flows.
summary: This theoretical paper distinguishes between two mathematical constraints—the pairing condition and the anomaly matching condition—that govern how symmetries and defects behave when mapping between $SU(N)$ WZW models. The authors demonstrate that the pairing condition is a stronger, canonical requirement necessary for a consistent description, suggesting it might be a more fundamental guiding principle than anomaly matching alone.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental difference between the 'pairing condition' derived from topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) and the 'anomaly matching condition' familiar from conformal field theories (CFTs) when mapping between $SU(N)$ WZW models.
main_result: The pairing condition provides a canonical relationship between symmetries and defects, which is shown to be intrinsically different and stronger than the condition derived solely from anomaly matching.
method: The analysis involves comparing constraints derived from simple current structures in TQFTs against anomaly matching requirements in CFTs, utilizing concepts from algebraic structures like $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries.
model_or_system: The primary models are $SU(N)_K$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) models, focusing on the reduction or mapping between models with different levels ($K$ and $K'$).
key_observables: The relationship between the levels $K$ and $K'$ modulo $N$, specifically comparing the pairing condition ($K = \pm R^2 K'$) versus the anomaly matching condition ($K = \pm R U K'$).
important_parameters: The level $K$ and $K'$ of the $SU(N)$ WZW models, and the integer $N$ defining the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing constraints derived from the folding trick/relative Deligne product ($ oxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_N}$) and the standard anomaly matching procedure.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the constraints from the pairing condition and then comparing these results to those obtained from the anomaly matching condition, culminating in a discussion of the implications of this mismatch.
why_interesting: The deep connection between symmetry protection, topological defects, and anomaly matching in highly symmetric quantum field theories provides a powerful, abstract framework applicable to understanding critical points in condensed matter systems.
